name: EDNRB (frame overo)
summary: EDNRB, endothelin receptor type B, on chromosome 17: part of a signalling pathway that both the pigment cells and the nerve cells of the gut depend on in the embryo. One two-base missense change, c.353_354delinsAG (p.Ile118Lys; g.50503041_50503042delinsCT on EquCab3.0), causes frame overo: big, sharp-edged white splotches across the middle of the side - barrel, flank, shoulder and lower neck - that never cross the back and rarely reach the belly, so colour is left framing them above and below. Broad white face, dark legs, and two sides that need not match; some carriers show almost nothing, which is why frame is tested for. The pattern is incompletely dominant and the lethal effect recessive: two copies (O/O) is Overo Lethal White - an all-white foal whose gut lacks its nerve supply and that does not survive. Found in Paint Horses, Quarter Horses, Thoroughbreds and other breeds with Paint ancestry. It has its locus to itself, so it stacks freely with every other white pattern.

phenotypes.name: Frame overo
phenotypes.description: Big, sharp-edged splotches of white across the middle of the side - barrel, flank, shoulder and lower neck - that never cross the back and rarely reach the belly, so the coloured coat is left framing them above and below, which is where the name comes from. The face is broadly white, often bald, and the legs stay dark but for the occasional coronet. The two sides need not match. Some carriers are marked so little you would never guess, which is why frame is tested for and not eyeballed.

phenotypes.name: Lethal white
phenotypes.description: An all-white foal with pink skin - Overo Lethal White Syndrome, which two frame carriers produce one time in four. The gut lacks its nerve supply, which is fatal: the foal is typically colicky within its first 12 hours and dies, or is put down, within the first few days.

conditions.name: Overo lethal white syndrome
conditions.description: Two frame copies. The foal is born almost wholly white, its gut lacks its nerve supply, and it dies of colic or is put down shortly after birth.

frequencies.population: American Paint Horse, Brazil (21.6% carry O, 89.5% of those classed as overo; 2018 study, sample size not given)
American Paint Horse, United States (10.7% of 180 horses carry O)
